paragraphs: Rav Zutra bar Tuvyah said in Rav’s name; Rav Zutra said in Rav’s name; Rav Zutra said in Rav’s name: Shabbat 75a. Rashi explains: he heard three things from Rav together and recited them. In the small Alfasi: “He heard these three things from Rav and recited them together.” Its wording implies he heard only these three things from Rav, therefore recited them together. He copied imprecisely: Rashi intended to exclude that explanation, and therefore delicately wrote, “He heard from Rav together and recited them.” For in Berakhot 6a, 43b we find several things he reported from Rav; also Pesachim 87a; Chagigah 12a, 13b; Bava Metzia 59a; Makkot 6b; Zevachim 64b. Why, then, were these three stated together? Because he heard them together from Rav. Understand this. Rav Zutra bar Tuvyah’s mother married Rav Zevid, who divorced her; she came before Rav Bibi bar Abaye: Bava Batra 151a. He recited the lesson before Rav Yehudah … and placed himself under censure for one day: Moed Katan 16b. He reported in Rav Nachman’s name: Yoma 86b.
